issues.description: The problem statement's UML (and the solution) expect a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient) instead. This name/signature mismatch is structural: students following the UML or the solution will attempt to call addToStockIngredients, which does not exist in the template, causing compilation errors or confusion.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the template Stock API match the UML/solution by renaming or adding the method addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient) in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Stock.java (and keep or alias addItem if desired). Alternatively, update the problem statement/UML to use addItem(StockIngredient) consistently.

issues.description: The problem statement UML and the solution implementation refer to a Stock method named addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), but the template Stock class provides a method named addItem(StockIngredient). This naming divergence for the same conceptual operation (adding a StockIngredient to the stock) can confuse students when mapping the UML/requirements to the starter code and the expected solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Either rename the template method addItem(StockIngredient) to addToStockIngredients(StockIngredient), or update the problem statement and solution to use addItem consistently. The preferred fix is to rename the template method to addToStockIngredients to match the UML and solution.
